envVars.name: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID

blocks.name: analytics-cf
blocks.description: Cloudflare Web Analytics integration for privacy-first analytics.

blocks.name: auth-better-auth
blocks.description: Authentication with Better Auth — email/password + OAuth providers, session management, and protected routes

envVars.name: AUTH_SECRET
envVars.description: Secret key for signing session tokens (generate with: openssl rand -hex 32)

ai.whenToUse: Use when the project needs user authentication — login, signup, session management, and protected routes. Better Auth supports email/password and OAuth providers (GitHub, Google, etc.).
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for public-only sites with no user accounts, or projects that need a different auth provider (e.g. Clerk, Auth0). Not suitable for static-only deployments.

blocks.name: blog-mdx
blocks.description: Full blog feature with MDX processing, listing page, post page, and RSS feed.

ai.whenToUse: User wants a blog powered by Markdown or MDX files. Generates a basic listing UI and dynamic slug routes for posts.
ai.whenNotToUse: User wants a headless CMS blog or doesn't need content features.

blocks.name: contact-form
blocks.description: Contact form section with name, email, subject, and message fields, powered by Astro Actions

ai.whenToUse: Use on any page that needs a contact form — landing pages, about pages, support pages. The form uses Astro Actions for server-side processing without a separate API.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use on fully static sites without a server adapter. Avoid if you only need an email link — a simple mailto: would suffice.

successMessage.example: Thank you! We'll get back to you soon.

blocks.name: cta-banner
blocks.description: Full-width call-to-action banner with headline, description, and prominent button for conversion

ai.whenToUse: Use between content sections or near the bottom of a page to drive a specific action. Best for trial signups, newsletter subscriptions, demo requests, or any page that needs a prominent conversion point.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use at the very top of a page (use a hero instead). Avoid stacking multiple CTA banners — one per page is ideal.

description.description: Supporting text that reinforces the value proposition
description.example: Join thousands of teams who ship faster with our platform.

blocks.name: cta-newsletter
blocks.description: Newsletter signup section with email input, headline, and description for building mailing lists

ai.whenToUse: Use when the page needs a newsletter or email capture section. Great for blogs, product landing pages, and content sites where building an email list is a priority.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use when the primary conversion goal is a product signup or purchase — use cta-banner instead. Avoid on pages that already have a prominent embed form.

description.description: Supporting text explaining what subscribers get

blocks.name: db-d1
blocks.description: Cloudflare D1 database integration with Drizzle ORM, migration support, and type-safe queries

envVars.name: D1_DATABASE_ID
envVars.description: Cloudflare D1 database ID from the Workers dashboard

ai.whenToUse: Use when the project needs a database for user data, content, or application state. D1 is Cloudflare's serverless SQLite database — ideal for edge-deployed Astro apps on Workers.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for static-only sites, purely client-side apps, or projects that already have a different database integration (turso, postgres). Not suitable for read-heavy workloads exceeding D1 limits.

blocks.name: docs-collection
blocks.description: Documentation feature with MDX processing and a generated sidebar navigation.

ai.whenToUse: User wants a documentation site powered by Markdown or MDX files with sidebar navigation.
ai.whenNotToUse: User wants a blog or headless CMS.

blocks.name: email-resend
blocks.description: Email sending integration using Resend.

ai.whenToUse: When the project requires sending transactional emails, such as magic links, receipts, or notifications.
ai.whenNotToUse: For purely static sites with no backend, or when using a different email provider.

blocks.name: faq-accordion
blocks.description: Expandable FAQ accordion with questions and answers using native HTML details/summary elements

ai.whenToUse: Use on pages that need an FAQ section — landing pages, pricing pages, product pages, or dedicated support pages. Best when you have 4-12 common questions to address.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for long-form documentation or knowledge bases. Avoid when answers are very short (a simple list would work better).

subheadline.example: Everything you need to know to get started.

example.question: How do I get started?
example.answer: Install the CLI with npm, run the init command, and our AI will guide you through setup in under 2 minutes.

example.question: Can I use my own components?
example.answer: Absolutely. Blocks are standard Astro components. You can customize them or create your own from scratch.

example.question: Is there a free tier?
example.answer: Yes! The CLI and all blocks are free and open source. We offer paid plans for premium AI features and priority support.

example.question: What deployment targets are supported?
example.answer: We support Cloudflare Workers, Pages, and Vercel out of the box. Custom adapters can be added for other platforms.

example.question: How does i18n work?
example.answer: Content is organized by locale in content collections. Add a locale and the AI generates culturally appropriate content automatically.

ai.whenToUse: Use when you want a modern, magazine-style feature showcase with asymmetric card sizes. Great for SaaS products, creative agencies, and tech companies that want visual variety over uniform grids.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use when features need equal visual weight or when you have fewer than 4 features. Avoid for documentation or content-heavy pages where a simple list is more appropriate.
